# Authoring with Portal Components

Read `docs/authoring.md` and `docs/components.md` before generating a page. `catalogue.generated.json` is the machine-readable source of valid props, types, enums, slots and exact working usage. `llms-full.txt` combines the maintained instructions/reference for one-context consumption.

## Hard rules

1. Write XML-shaped HTML with `xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml"`. Close void elements in source: `<input/>`.
2. Invoke `<portal-component name="button">`. Pass literal props with `<portal-prop name="variant" value="secondary"/>`; pass typed data with `<portal-prop name="disabled" t:value="input.disabled"/>`. Do not invent Vue bindings, JS expressions or direct prop attributes.
3. Unnamed children fill the default slot. Named content uses `<portal-fill name="footer">`. Caller slots keep caller scope; component internals only receive `props`, slot-presence flags and `component.id`.
4. Only use props and slots listed in the component contract. Names/enum values are exact. Use `t:value="true"` / `t:value="false"` for boolean constants and `t:value="65"` for numeric constants; `value` always supplies a string. Dynamic values must have the declared type.
5. Components do not fetch or mutate. Keep Lua in page/server handlers and use normal protected page forms. No `<script>`, onclick, client Lua or arbitrary networking.
6. Use real HTML labels, control ids, names and native form semantics. Set button type=submit intentionally. Provide unique ids for repeated controls, and match `for`/`describedby` exactly.
7. Internal URLs use the standard Portal mount-aware helpers/HTML handling. Do not hardcode a staff-preview prefix.
8. Brand with documented `--portal-*` variables. To change markup copy the complete `.html` and `.json` pair locally; do not edit the host bundle.
9. Do not infer upload, sorting, payment, dialog, tabs, client state or combobox functionality from visual markup. Read each component's limits.
10. Compile the result with the real Portal compiler. A plausible-looking snippet is not evidence it compiles.

## Recommended workflow

Choose components from the catalogue, build the semantic native page first, then connect page Lua and progressive regions. Include complete namespaces and contracts in standalone examples. Keep fetched view models serializable and keep repeated presentation components free of loaders. Verify native no-JavaScript behavior, errors, empty results, mobile layout and keyboard use.

If an API is missing from this documentation, say so instead of inventing it. Components are not a general Vue-compatible environment.

## Complete page compositions

Use `docs/layouts.md` for sign-in, print catalogue, order tracking and order request recipes. Each includes full DataXML source and integration notes. Copy `styles/layouts.css` after bundled styles; theme tokens remain inherited. These are static layouts with fictional content and disabled business actions, not working authentication, filtering, uploading or checkout. Do not remove disabled actions without wiring the appropriate protected Portal flow. Reuse components and native HTML; do not invent client scripts or handler capabilities from a screenshot.


# Authoring contract

## Props

Literal values are supplied through `portal-prop` children:

```xml
<portal-component name="button">
  <portal-prop name="variant" value="secondary"/>
  <portal-prop name="disabled" t:value="true"/>
  Save draft
</portal-component>
```

Dynamic values use the existing DataXML expression evaluator:

```xml
<portal-component name="badge">
  <portal-prop name="variant" t:value="data.statusVariant"/>
  <span t:text="data.statusLabel"/>
</portal-component>
```

A string, number or boolean stays that type; values are validated before rendering. Defaults apply when a prop is absent. Explicit null is accepted only when declared nullable. Unknown props, invalid types/enums and missing required values are errors. Do not use direct attributes such as `<portal-component variant="secondary">`.

## Slots and isolation

Unnamed children fill the default slot. `portal-fill` selects a declared named slot. Content runs in the caller's lexical scope; a child's template sees its own props, `slots.<name>` presence flags and `component.id`, not caller data or credentials. Empty supplied slots suppress fallback content. Named fills are not separate components and cannot fetch data.

A component source has one root and uses `portal-outlet`:

```xml
<section xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml">
  <header t:if="slots.header"><portal-outlet name="header"/></header>
  <portal-outlet name="default"><p>No content supplied.</p></portal-outlet>
</section>
```

The corresponding contract is a separate JSON file:

```json
{
  "props": {},
  "slots": { "header": { "required": false }, "default": { "required": false } }
}
```

This illustrates a local custom component, not a replacement for the richer bundled Card. Unknown slots, duplicate named fills and incomplete local file pairs fail validation.

## Native forms

Use a caller-owned form and page-owned action handler. The handler must be declared in the page/site contract; components do not register it implicitly.

```xml
<form xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" data-portal-action="saveContact">
  <portal-component name="field">
    <portal-prop name="for" value="customer-email"/>
    <portal-prop name="label" value="Email address"/>
    <portal-component name="input">
      <portal-prop name="id" value="customer-email"/>
      <portal-prop name="name" value="email"/>
      <portal-prop name="type" value="email"/>
      <portal-prop name="autocomplete" value="email"/>
      <portal-prop name="required" t:value="true"/>
    </portal-component>
  </portal-component>
  <portal-component name="button">
    <portal-prop name="type" value="submit"/>
    Save contact
  </portal-component>
</form>
```

The Portal host adds protected action routing and form fences. Server-side authorization and validation remain required. Use a native GET form with an ordinary action for filtering. The showcase can demonstrate native controls but cannot execute an instance's business APIs.

## IDs, keys and overrides

Pass stable, unique IDs for form controls and association references. A component's internal generated identity does not leak into caller slot scope. Prefer page view models containing precomputed IDs when rendering repeated fields; never reuse one literal id in a loop. Component invocation keys identify repeated siblings; they do not authorize access or replace explicit HTML form IDs.

To override Card, copy both `components/card.html` and `components/card.json` to your site's same paths. Local resolution takes precedence. Keep all required slots/props expected by existing callers or change those callers. There is no automatic update merge or CLI installer in v1.

## Frequent errors

| Incorrect | Correct |
| --- | --- |
| `<Button variant="primary">` | `<portal-component name="button"><portal-prop name="variant" value="primary"/>…</portal-component>` |
| `:disabled="loading"` | `<portal-prop name="disabled" t:value="input.loading"/>` with a boolean |
| `<template #footer>` | `<portal-fill name="footer">…</portal-fill>` |
| `onclick="save()"` | A page-owned protected native form action |
| A component reads `data.customer` implicitly | Pass a declared prop from the caller |
| Copy only component HTML | Copy the `.html` and `.json` pair |
| A placeholder used instead of a label | A visible label associated with the input id |

Scoped slots, automatic client hydration and component-owned Lua loaders are not v1 features. The source/contract model leaves room for later extensions without inventing them today.

## Repeated fields with descriptions and errors

Give the page loader a view model containing unique association IDs. For example, `data.lines` can contain:

```json
[
  {"key":"line-42","controlId":"quantity-42","descriptionId":"quantity-42-hint","errorId":"quantity-42-error","describedby":"quantity-42-hint quantity-42-error","quantity":"0","error":"Enter at least 1","invalid":true}
]
```

Use a keyed invocation inside the DataXML loop:

```xml
<section xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml">
  <div t:for="data.lines" t:as="line">
    <portal-component name="field" t:attr-key="line.key">
      <portal-prop name="for" t:value="line.controlId"/>
      <portal-prop name="label" value="Quantity"/>
      <portal-prop name="description" value="Minimum 1 item"/>
      <portal-prop name="descriptionId" t:value="line.descriptionId"/>
      <portal-prop name="error" t:value="line.error"/>
      <portal-prop name="errorId" t:value="line.errorId"/>
      <portal-component name="input">
        <portal-prop name="id" t:value="line.controlId"/>
        <portal-prop name="name" t:value="line.controlId"/>
        <portal-prop name="type" value="number"/>
        <portal-prop name="min" value="1"/>
        <portal-prop name="value" t:value="line.quantity"/>
        <portal-prop name="invalid" t:value="line.invalid"/>
        <portal-prop name="describedby" t:value="line.describedby"/>
      </portal-component>
    </portal-component>
  </div>
</section>
```

The caller slot can still read `line`; it cannot read Field's private props. Keep the `describedby` list limited to elements actually rendered: omit the error ID when there is no error. The input value remains a string even when its HTML type is number; validate/coerce native form input on the server. This example deliberately uses unique control names because repeated-name collection behavior belongs to the form handler contract, not the component library.


# Theme tokens

Add `portal-theme` to the site content root. The supplied stylesheet has no global reset, remote fonts or mandatory CSS framework. Tokens inherit through components. The default theme is light; `data-theme="dark"` and `data-theme="atelier"` select bundled examples.

```css
/* Place after the bundled styles. */
.portal-theme.my-brand {
  --portal-primary: #145744;
  --portal-primary-content: #ffffff;
  --portal-focus: #145744;
  --portal-radius-md: .25rem;
  --portal-font-family: Georgia, serif;
}
```

For a local override, set a token on a wrapper around a component. Do not add a second `portal-theme` class on every nested element: that resets the defaults at each new theme root. Copy a component when you need different structure or selectors.

Colour pairs must be checked together. The default themes supply text/background pairs; a custom token can break contrast or focus visibility. Preserve native semantics and test high contrast/forced-colour mode. `prefers-reduced-motion` sets the motion-duration token to zero. V1 components do not rely on animation.

See [the generated token reference](tokens.md) for all exact names/defaults. Typography, spacing, border, radius and content-width tokens are site-wide defaults; the library deliberately avoids an undocumented variable for every declaration.

## Branding contract

Set tokens on the theme root after the bundled stylesheet. The same rules work
with a named theme: `.portal-theme.my-brand` has the same specificity as a bundled
`data-theme` selector, so the later author stylesheet wins. Inline custom
properties also work. Existing published sites retain their captured library CSS.

| Area | Main controls |
| --- | --- |
| Surfaces and text | `--portal-canvas`, `--portal-surface`, `--portal-surface-muted`, `--portal-text`, `--portal-text-muted` |
| Semantic colours | `primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, with matching `-content` foreground tokens (all prefixed `--portal-`) |
| Body typography | `--portal-font-family`, `--portal-font-mono`, `--portal-font-size`, `--portal-font-size-xs/sm/lg/xl`, `--portal-line-height`, `--portal-letter-spacing`, `--portal-font-weight-normal/medium/bold` |
| Headings | `--portal-heading-font-family`, `--portal-heading-font-weight`, `--portal-heading-line-height`, `--portal-heading-letter-spacing`, `--portal-heading-size-1` through `-6` |
| Form controls | `--portal-control-font-family`, `--portal-control-font-size`, `--portal-control-font-weight`, `--portal-control-line-height`, `--portal-control-height` and `-sm/-lg`, `--portal-choice-size` |
| Borders and shape | `--portal-border`, `--portal-border-width`, `--portal-border-style`, `--portal-border-width-strong/accent`, `--portal-radius-sm/md/lg/pill` |
| Elevation | `--portal-shadow` (cards), `--portal-shadow-control`, `--portal-shadow-button`, `--portal-shadow-overlay` (available for authored compositions) |
| Focus and disabled state | `--portal-focus`, `--portal-focus-width`, `--portal-focus-offset`, `--portal-disabled-opacity` |
| Layout | `--portal-space-*`, `--portal-content-width`, `--portal-reading-width` |

Semantic tokens are available for authored content as well as library components;
not every colour role has a built-in component variant. For example, `accent` and
its content pair can style a branded callout without introducing new markup APIs.
Heading font defaults to inheritance; heading size tokens apply to ordinary h1–h6
inside the theme. Component-specific small headings use the size scale (`lg`/`xl`).
Controls inherit body typography unless their control tokens are changed.

```css
.portal-theme.my-brand {
  --portal-primary: #145744;
  --portal-primary-content: #ffffff;
  --portal-font-family: Georgia, serif;
  --portal-font-size: 1.125rem;
  --portal-line-height: 1.6;
  --portal-heading-font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
  --portal-heading-font-weight: 700;
  --portal-heading-letter-spacing: -.02em;
  --portal-heading-size-1: 2.5rem;
  --portal-control-font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
  --portal-border-width: 2px;
  --portal-border-style: solid;
  --portal-radius-md: .25rem;
  --portal-radius-lg: .5rem;
  --portal-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgb(20 87 68 / 12%);
  --portal-shadow-control: inset 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 8%);
  --portal-focus-width: 3px;
  --portal-focus-offset: 4px;
}
```

Optional per-component overrides are resolved where used, so they also work on a
wrapper inside an existing theme: `--portal-button-background`/`--portal-button-color`
(primary buttons), `--portal-input-background`/`--portal-input-color`, and
`--portal-card-shadow`. They fall back to the semantic tokens; they are not required
root declarations. A wrapper can also override the shared tokens directly.
Forced-colour mode deliberately retains system-colour borders rather than allowing
brand borders to remove essential affordances. Custom themes remain responsible for
contrast; full shadow strings can be set to `none` for a flat design. No font is
fetched automatically: use available system fonts or provide an allowed font asset.

# Component reference

Generated from catalogue.json, component contracts and executable example source. Do not edit this file directly. Library 0.1.1, contract 1.

## button

A native button with explicit type and visual emphasis.

Source: [template](../components/button.html) · [contract](../components/button.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | string | `"button"` | `button`, `submit`, `reset` |
| `variant` | string | `"primary"` | `primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `danger` |
| `size` | string | `"md"` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | — |
| `name` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `value` | string or null | omitted | — |

Slots:

- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <div style="display:flex;gap:1rem;flex-wrap:wrap">
    <portal-component name="button">Continue</portal-component>
    <portal-component name="button">
      <portal-prop name="variant" value="secondary"/>
      Save draft
    </portal-component>
  </div>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Uses a real button. Choose type="submit" inside a form; the default button never submits accidentally. Disabled buttons remain native disabled controls. Visible text supplies the accessible name.

## link

A native navigation link with optional visual emphasis.

Source: [template](../components/link.html) · [contract](../components/link.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | string | required | — |
| `variant` | string | `"text"` | `text`, `button` |
| `label` | string or null | omitted | — |

Slots:

- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="link">
    <portal-prop name="href" value="#details"/>
    View order
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Use meaningful link text. Internal hrefs receive ordinary Portal mount resolution. Do not use this as a fake disabled button.

## badge

A compact textual status marker.

Source: [template](../components/badge.html) · [contract](../components/badge.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | string | `"neutral"` | `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` |

Slots:

- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="badge">
    <portal-prop name="variant" value="success"/>
    Ready for print
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Text communicates status; colour is supplementary. This component does not announce changes as a live region.

## card

A panel with optional header and footer.

Source: [template](../components/card.html) · [contract](../components/card.json)

No props.

Slots:

- `default`: optional
- `header`: optional
- `footer`: optional

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="card">
    <portal-fill name="header">
      <h2>Business cards</h2>
    </portal-fill>
    <p>Premium stock, printed with care.</p>
    <portal-fill name="footer">
      <p>From £24</p>
    </portal-fill>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Choose heading levels in caller content to match the page hierarchy; Card does not force an h2 or region label.

## alert

A static notice with optional heading and actions.

Source: [template](../components/alert.html) · [contract](../components/alert.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | string | `"info"` | `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` |

Slots:

- `default`: required
- `title`: optional
- `actions`: optional

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="alert">
    <portal-prop name="variant" value="warning"/>
    <portal-fill name="title">
      <strong>Artwork needs attention</strong>
    </portal-fill>
    <p>Please upload a PDF with embedded fonts.</p>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Static notices do not use role=alert, avoiding unsolicited announcements on page load. Dynamic error announcements require the host runtime contract.


Preserve semantic HTML and visible focus styles when customizing.

## grid

A responsive grid that collapses on narrow screens.

Source: [template](../components/grid.html) · [contract](../components/grid.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | string | `"3"` | `2`, `3`, `4` |
| `gap` | string | `"md"` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` |

Slots:

- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="grid">
    <div class="portal-demo-box">One</div>
    <div class="portal-demo-box">Two</div>
    <div class="portal-demo-box">Three</div>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

DOM order remains reading and keyboard order. Do not use CSS to change meaningful content order.

## field

A label, description and error wrapper for an explicitly identified control.

Source: [template](../components/field.html) · [contract](../components/field.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `for` | string | required | — |
| `label` | string | required | — |
| `description` | string | `""` | — |
| `error` | string | `""` | — |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | — |
| `descriptionId` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `errorId` | string or null | omitted | — |

Slots:

- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="field">
    <portal-prop name="for" value="contact-name"/>
    <portal-prop name="label" value="Your name"/>
    <portal-prop name="required" t:value="true"/>
    <portal-component name="input">
      <portal-prop name="id" value="contact-name"/>
      <portal-prop name="name" value="name"/>
      <portal-prop name="autocomplete" value="name"/>
      <portal-prop name="required" t:value="true"/>
    </portal-component>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

The for prop must equal the nested control id. Also set required on the control. When using description/error, provide descriptionId/errorId and pass those same ids to the nested control describedby prop (space-separated if both). Mark the control invalid=true for an error. IDs must be unique in the document.

## input

A native single-line input with label/error association.

Source: [template](../components/input.html) · [contract](../components/input.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | required | — |
| `name` | string | required | — |
| `value` | string | `""` | — |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | — |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | — |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | — |
| `describedby` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `autocomplete` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `type` | string | `"text"` | `text`, `email`, `tel`, `url`, `number`, `password`, `search`, `date`, `time`, `datetime-local`, `month`, `week`, `color`, `range` |
| `placeholder` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `readonly` | boolean | `false` | — |
| `inputmode` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `min` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `max` | string or null | omitted | — |
| `step` | string or null | omitted | — |

Slots:

None.

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <label for="email-example">Email address</label>
  <portal-component name="input">
    <portal-prop name="id" value="email-example"/>
    <portal-prop name="name" value="email"/>
    <portal-prop name="type" value="email"/>
    <portal-prop name="autocomplete" value="email"/>
    <portal-prop name="placeholder" value="you@example.com"/>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Always provide a visible associated label. Placeholder is not a label. Pass a unique id for each repeated control. File inputs do not gain upload capability from this component.

## disclosure

Native details/summary disclosure without JavaScript.

Source: [template](../components/disclosure.html) · [contract](../components/disclosure.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | boolean | `false` | — |

- `default`: required

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
```

## table

A semantic table with caption and caller-owned header/body rows.

Source: [template](../components/table.html) · [contract](../components/table.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `caption` | string | required | — |

Slots:

- `head`: optional
- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="table">
    <portal-prop name="caption" value="Recent orders"/>
    <portal-fill name="head">
      <tr>
        <th scope="col">Order</th>
        <th scope="col">Status</th>
      </tr>
    </portal-fill>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">#1042</th>
      <td>In production</td>
    </tr>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Use tr elements in slots and appropriate th scope attributes. The caption is visible. The labelled wrapper is keyboard-focusable so overflowing columns can be scrolled with arrow keys. No sorting, row selection or grid keyboard model is implied.

## breadcrumbs

A labelled breadcrumb navigation list.

Source: [template](../components/breadcrumbs.html) · [contract](../components/breadcrumbs.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | string | `"Breadcrumb"` | — |

Slots:

- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="breadcrumbs">
    <li>
      <a href="#home">Home</a>
    </li>
    <li>
      <span aria-current="page">Orders</span>
    </li>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Supply li items. Mark the current page with aria-current=page and use text rather than a redundant active link. Separators are decorative CSS.

## pagination

A labelled container for page navigation.

Source: [template](../components/pagination.html) · [contract](../components/pagination.json)

| Prop | Type | Default | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | string | `"Pagination"` | — |

Slots:

- `default`: required

### Usage

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-example">
  <portal-component name="pagination">
    <li>
      <span aria-disabled="true">Previous</span>
    </li>
    <li>
      <a href="?page=1" aria-current="page" aria-label="Page 1">1</a>
    </li>
    <li>
      <a href="?page=2" aria-label="Page 2">2</a>
    </li>
    <li>
      <a href="?page=2">Next</a>
    </li>
  </portal-component>
</main>
```

### Accessibility and limits

Supply li items and real hrefs. Use non-links for unavailable actions and aria-current=page for the current page. No client-only pagination state.

## skeleton

A decorative placeholder for an explicitly labelled loading region.

Source: [template](../components/skeleton.html) · [contract](../components/skeleton.json)

# Page layout recipes

Complete, themeable compositions rendered by the production Portal renderer. These are documentation recipes, not connected starter portals. All people, addresses, orders and prices are fictional. No login, filtering, upload or business mutation is connected.

Copy the DataXML and [layout CSS](../styles/layouts.css), loading it after the bundled component styles. Keep the `portal-theme portal-layout` wrapper. The CSS uses inherited semantic tokens, so the same theme applies to components and layout. Replace illustrative actions with protected Portal flows; never activate them by simply removing `disabled`.

## Sign in

A welcoming account entry point with a branded panel, labelled fields and recovery guidance.

Components: `card`, `field`, `input`, `button`, `disclosure`.

Use your Portal authentication flow; never put credentials in query strings or client storage. The demo has no form or authentication endpoint. Fields are illustrative and the action is disabled.

[DataXML source](../examples/layout-sign-in.html) · [Rendered example](../rendered/layout-sign-in.html)

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-layout layout-sign-in">
  <header class="recipe-header">
    <a class="recipe-brand" href="#page-content">
      <span aria-hidden="true">p.</span>
       Paper &amp; Form
    </a>
    <span class="recipe-header-label">Customer portal</span>
  </header>
  <div class="login-layout" id="page-content">
    <section class="login-story">
      <p class="recipe-kicker">YOUR NEXT GREAT IMPRESSION</p>
      <h1>
        Good ideas.
        <br/>
        Beautifully printed.
      </h1>
      <p>One place for your print projects, proofs and deliveries. A little less admin. A lot more possibility.</p>
      <div class="print-art print-art-cards" aria-hidden="true">
        <div class="print-sheet">
          <span>Paper &amp; Form</span>
          <strong>
            Make
            <br/>
            your mark.
          </strong>
          <i>Made to make an impression.</i>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="story-facts">
        <span>Thoughtfully made</span>
        <span>From first proof to final print</span>
      </div>
    </section>
    <section class="login-panel" aria-labelledby="login-title">
      <div>
        <p class="recipe-kicker">WELCOME BACK</p>
        <h2 id="login-title">Your projects start here.</h2>
        <p class="recipe-muted">Sign in to your Paper &amp; Form account.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="recipe-fields" role="group" aria-label="Example sign-in fields">
        <portal-component name="field">
          <portal-prop name="for" value="email"/>
          <portal-prop name="label" value="Email address"/>
          <portal-component name="input">
            <portal-prop name="id" value="email"/>
            <portal-prop name="name" value="email"/>
            <portal-prop name="type" value="email"/>
            <portal-prop name="value" value=""/>
            <portal-prop name="placeholder" value="you@company.com"/>
            <portal-prop name="autocomplete" value="off"/>
          </portal-component>
        </portal-component>
        <portal-component name="field">
          <portal-prop name="for" value="password"/>
          <portal-prop name="label" value="Password"/>
          <portal-component name="input">
            <portal-prop name="id" value="password"/>
            <portal-prop name="name" value="password"/>
            <portal-prop name="type" value="password"/>
            <portal-prop name="value" value=""/>
            <portal-prop name="autocomplete" value="off"/>
          </portal-component>
        </portal-component>
        <p class="recipe-muted recipe-small">Demo only. Please do not enter real credentials.</p>
        <portal-component name="button">
          <portal-prop name="disabled" t:value="true"/>
          <portal-prop name="size" value="lg"/>
          Sign in
        </portal-component>
      </div>
      <portal-component name="disclosure">
        <portal-fill name="summary">Need help signing in?</portal-fill>
        <p>In your portal, link this section to password recovery or your customer support team. This example has no authentication service.</p>
      </portal-component>
      <p class="recipe-small recipe-muted">New to Paper &amp; Form? Your account contact can invite you to the customer portal.</p>
      <p class="recipe-demo-note">Sample layout · Fictional data · Business actions are disabled</p>
    </section>
  </div>
</main>
```

## Print catalogue

A responsive product collection with filters, sorting and a distinctive editorial product grid.

Components: `card`, `field`, `input`, `select`, `checkbox`, `badge`, `button`.

Replace the six synthetic products with Lua loader output. Keep filter controls outside the results region; use a native GET form and a targeted live region when connecting search. This static example does not filter or navigate products.

```xml
            <portal-prop name="checked" t:value="false"/>
            Business stationery
          </portal-component>
          <portal-component name="checkbox">
            <portal-prop name="name" value="category"/>
            <portal-prop name="value" value="marketing"/>
            <portal-prop name="checked" t:value="false"/>
            Marketing &amp; events
          </portal-component>
          <portal-component name="checkbox">

            <portal-prop name="value" value="packaging"/>
            <portal-prop name="checked" t:value="false"/>

          </portal-component>
        </div>
      </portal-component>

    </aside>
    <section aria-labelledby="products-title">
```

## Order tracking

A clear production timeline, delivery details and an itemised order summary.

Components: `card`, `badge`, `table`, `disclosure`.

Fetch the order through an authorised Lua read handler scoped to the current PortalUser and customer membership. Treat the order reference as an identifier, not permission to view an order. Tracking and totals here are fictional.

[DataXML source](../examples/layout-order-tracking.html) · [Rendered example](../rendered/layout-order-tracking.html)

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-layout layout-order-tracking">
  <header class="recipe-header">
    <a class="recipe-brand" href="#page-content">

       Paper &amp; Form
    </a>

  </header>

    <div class="recipe-page-heading">

      </div>

        In production
      </portal-component>
    </div>

              <span class="timeline-dot" aria-hidden="true">✓</span>

              </div>

              <span class="timeline-dot" aria-hidden="true">✓</span>

                <h3>Artwork approved</h3>
                <p>05 Nov · Proof confirmed by Alex Morgan.</p>
              </div>
            </li>
            <li aria-current="step">
              <span class="timeline-dot" aria-hidden="true">3</span>
```

## Order request

A guided product configuration with artwork guidance and an adjacent quote summary.

Components: `card`, `field`, `input`, `select`, `badge`, `alert`, `button`, `disclosure`.

Keep editable configuration outside the replaceable quote region. Calculate and validate prices on the server. Wire submission to a protected Lua action; group related writes in the platform transaction capability. Connect authorised Folder uploads separately; this sample does not accept files or orders.

[DataXML source](../examples/layout-order-request.html) · [Rendered example](../rendered/layout-order-request.html)

```xml
<main xmlns:t="urn:cococo:dataxml" class="portal-theme portal-layout layout-order-request">
  <header class="recipe-header">
    <a class="recipe-brand" href="#page-content">
      <span aria-hidden="true">p.</span>
       Paper &amp; Form
    </a>
    <span class="recipe-header-label">Create a print order</span>
  </header>
  <div class="recipe-content" id="page-content">
    <p class="recipe-kicker">SMALL DETAILS. BIG IMPRESSION.</p>
    <h1>Make it your business card.</h1>
    <p class="recipe-muted">Choose the finish, feel and format. We’ll take care of the print.</p>
    <div class="request-layout">
      <div class="recipe-stack">
        <div class="print-art print-art-cards" aria-hidden="true">
          <div class="print-sheet">
            <span>Paper &amp; Form</span>
            <strong>
              Studio
              <br/>
              North.
            </strong>
            <i>Made to make an impression.</i>
          </div>
        </div>
        <portal-component name="card">
          <portal-fill name="header">
            <h2>01 · The details</h2>
          </portal-fill>
          <div class="recipe-fields">
            <div class="recipe-field-grid">
              <portal-component name="field">
                <portal-prop name="for" value="size"/>
                <portal-prop name="label" value="Finished size"/>
                <portal-component name="select">
                  <portal-prop name="id" value="size"/>
                  <portal-prop name="name" value="size"/>
                  <option>85 × 55 mm · Standard</option>
                  <option>55 × 55 mm · Square</option>
                </portal-component>
              </portal-component>
              <portal-component name="field">
                <portal-prop name="for" value="paper"/>
                <portal-prop name="label" value="Paper &amp; finish"/>
                <portal-component name="select">
                  <portal-prop name="id" value="paper"/>
                  <portal-prop name="name" value="paper"/>
                  <option>450gsm · Soft-touch</option>
                  <option>350gsm · Uncoated</option>
                </portal-component>
              </portal-component>
              <portal-component name="field">
                <portal-prop name="for" value="quantity"/>
                <portal-prop name="label" value="Quantity"/>
                <portal-component name="input">
                  <portal-prop name="id" value="quantity"/>
                  <portal-prop name="name" value="quantity"/>
                  <portal-prop name="type" value="number"/>
                  <portal-prop name="value" value="500"/>
                  <portal-prop name="min" value="250"/>
                  <portal-prop name="step" value="250"/>
                  <portal-prop name="max" value="10000"/>
                </portal-component>
              </portal-component>
              <portal-component name="field">
                <portal-prop name="for" value="printing"/>
                <portal-prop name="label" value="Printing"/>
                <portal-component name="select">
                  <portal-prop name="id" value="printing"/>
                  <portal-prop name="name" value="printing"/>
                  <option>Double-sided colour</option>
                  <option>Single-sided colour</option>
                </portal-component>
              </portal-component>
            </div>
            <portal-component name="field">
              <portal-prop name="for" value="reference"/>
              <portal-prop name="label" value="Your project reference"/>
              <portal-component name="input">
                <portal-prop name="id" value="reference"/>
                <portal-prop name="name" value="reference"/>
                <portal-prop name="type" value="text"/>
                <portal-prop name="value" value="Autumn studio collection"/>
              </portal-component>
            </portal-component>
          </div>
        </portal-component>
        <portal-component name="card">
          <portal-fill name="header">
            <h2>02 · Your artwork</h2>
          </portal-fill>
          <p>Supply a print-ready PDF with 3 mm bleed. Keep important details at least 4 mm from the trim edge.</p>
          <portal-component name="alert">
            <portal-prop name="variant" value="info"/>
            This static example has no upload service. Connect your portal’s authorised Folder upload flow before accepting artwork.
          </portal-component>
          <portal-component name="disclosure">
            <portal-fill name="summary">Artwork checklist</portal-fill>
            <ul>
              <li>CMYK colour, with images at 300 dpi.</li>
              <li>Fonts embedded or converted to outlines.</li>
              <li>Front and back supplied as separate PDF pages.</li>
            </ul>
          </portal-component>
        </portal-component>
      </div>
      <aside class="recipe-stack request-summary" aria-label="Example quote">
        <portal-component name="card">
          <p class="recipe-kicker">YOUR PRINT, AT A GLANCE</p>
          <h2>Business cards</h2>
          <p class="recipe-muted">
            500 cards · 85 × 55 mm
            <br/>
            450gsm soft-touch · Double-sided
          </p>
          <portal-component name="badge">
            <portal-prop name="variant" value="neutral"/>
            Sample quote
          </portal-component>
          <dl class="summary-list">
            <div>
              <dt>Printing</dt>
              <dd>£48.00</dd>
            </div>
            <div>
              <dt>Standard delivery</dt>
              <dd>£6.00</dd>
            </div>
            <div>
              <dt>VAT (20%)</dt>
              <dd>£10.80</dd>
            </div>
            <div class="summary-total">
              <dt>Total</dt>
              <dd>£64.80</dd>
            </div>
          </dl>
          <p class="recipe-small recipe-muted">Estimated dispatch in 3–5 working days after artwork approval.</p>
          <portal-component name="button">
            <portal-prop name="disabled" t:value="true"/>
            <portal-prop name="size" value="lg"/>
            Review your order
          </portal-component>
          <p class="recipe-small recipe-muted">Illustrative pricing. Changing options does not recalculate this sample quote.</p>
        </portal-component>
        <portal-component name="disclosure">
          <portal-fill name="summary">What happens next?</portal-fill>
          <p>In a connected portal, the server recalculates your quote and validates artwork before accepting your order. Always confirm the final price before payment.</p>
        </portal-component>
      </aside>
    </div>
    <p class="recipe-demo-note">Sample layout · Fictional data · Business actions are disabled</p>
  </div>
</main>
```
